frequency_question: How often do states successfully establish domestic production lines for advanced transferred missile technology within a tight timeline?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign nations transitioning from importing complex foreign missile systems to domestic assembly or manufacture during active conflict or severe crisis. Excludes standard peacetime domestic defense procurement without technology transfer.

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile series (US technology transfer/domestic production)
India BrahMos joint venture (Russian-Indian missile co-production)
Ukraine Neptune missile domestic serial production ramp-up
Iran Soumar/Qods cruise missile reverse engineering and production
South Korea Hyunmoo missile domestic production expansion

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named; representative of high-stakes defense localization cases.
known_gaps: Does not fully account for micro-component supply chain blockages belonging to non-will factors.
skeleton: 6 historical high-tech missile localization efforts examined under urgent state security imperatives.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 relevant instances of intense state will and supplier-backed technical transfer.
validity_reason: Defense industrial base practices and urgent wartime localization dynamics remain consistent across modern state conflicts.
